General Henri Joseph Eugene Gourand, a lean grizzled veteran of 56, with five wound stripes and an empty sleeve, who stepped ashore in New York City, from the SS France on his first visit to America. The French hero received an aviation that has rarely been accorded to a foreigner.

He was doubly welcomed as one of the gallant figures of the war and as commander of various American units in France.

GENERAL JOFFRE AND MILITARY ALDES
Officers lined up with French hero of the Marne Who is Cheered by U. S. Crowds.

General Joffre, French Marshall and hero of the Marne, and party were accorded a tremendous ovation upon their arrival in Washington. Crowds cheered them wherever they appeared. The photograph shows the hero and his military aides leaving the State's Department Building:

Reading from left to right, the officers of the group are: General Luval; of the French Army. Lt. Spencer Cosby, U.S.A.; General Joffre; Lieut. U.S. Grant,3rd, U.S.A.; Lt. Pesson, of the French army, and Colonel Fabri (with cane) also of the French Army.

MARSHAL JOFFRE OFF ON TOUR OF U. S.
Marstar Joseph Joffre, popular idol and America's guest, in a unusual and striking photograph made recently in Washington, D.C.

"Papa" Joffre, as he is familiarly known, left the Capital today with other members of the French Commission for a tour of the Middle West and the East. They will stop at the cities of Chicago, St. Louis, and Springfield, Ill., where they will visit the tomb of Lincoln. They will then journey on to Philadelphia, New York, and Boston, returning to Washington.

ALLIED DELEGATIONS PROCEED TO BOULOGNE.

The British, French and Greek delegations crossed the Channel yesterday for the Conference at Beulegne, where they meet representatives of Belgium, Italy and Japan. The vital points at issue are understood to be the disarrament of Germany, the payment of her indemnity debt and the Turkish situation.

Our photo shows, Marshall Feb leaving Villa Belle in his car after the first sitting.
FRANCE'S FAREWELL TO OUR UNKNOWN WARRIOR...MOVING SCENES AT BOULOGNE.

Moving beyond expression was France's parting with our Unknown Warriors to-day Ved 10th 1920. Marshal Foch marched behind the coffin, which was covered by a Union Jack. The body, chosen from twenty taken from the scattered cemeteries of France, lay all night in an historic 13th century Chateau in Boulogne. It was set in a church which was a bower of flowers. In the dusk of the late afternoon, he, who symbolises the Empire's countless dead, was landed at Dover to receive the Empire's homage, and to rest among her immortal sons in Westminster Abbey.

JULES BOIS, ENVOY OF GRATITUDE, SENT HERE BY THE FRENCH GOVERNMENT.

Jules Bois, on the deck of the French liner Reohambeau which arrived yesterday.

Jules Bois, distinguished French post, dramatist, and journalist, arrived on the French liner Reohambeau, on a "mission of Sentiment", as he described it, to distinguish it from the missions of many of his compatriots who have preceded him. The French Government as a special mark of appreciation, will permit the entire company of the Theatre Frances to visit this country next October. For the first time since the founding of the institution in 1681, the French Government has agreed that the organization may leave France. Mr. Bois also comes to arrange for the education in this country of many young Frenchmen who will serve apprenticeships in the great banking houses of the country, in our mills, and in our experimental farms and colleges. ALSATIANS WELCOME BLUMENTHAL, SPECIAL FRENCH ENVOY TO U.S.

Daniel Blumenthal, former Mayor of Colmar, Alsace Lorraine, was given an official welcome at Apolian Hall under the auspices of Les Amis de l'Alsace-Lorraine, in celebration of the French National holiday, July 14th.

Mr. Blumenthal is a special envoy to this country from the French Government, his mission being to make known the policy of Germany toward the "lost provinces" and to urge that their restoration to France be made a condition of peace at the end of the war.

ISLAND SOLD FOR 22,400,000.

Senator Gaston Monier, the French "Chocolate King" completed yesterday the sale of Anticosti Island in the Gulf of St. Lawrence for the sum of £2,400,000. The purchasers are the Anticosti Corporation. The Island has an area of 3,320 square miles, and M. Menier insisted that the payment should be made in cash as he desired to make a substantial gift to save the franc. O.P.S. Senator Gaston Monier.
